cards.b: Bit = one binary digit (0 or 1). Nibble = 4 bits. Byte = 8 bits.
128, 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1. Each column is double the one to its right.

cards.f: How many values can n bits store?
cards.b: 2ⁿ different values. 8 bits give 256 values (0 to 255 unsigned).

cards.f: How many bits does one hex digit represent?
cards.b: 4 bits (a nibble). Split binary into groups of 4 from the right to convert to hex.
Shorter and easier for humans to read, remember and copy than binary, so fewer mistakes. Converts easily to binary.
The result of a calculation is too big to fit in the available bits, so the stored answer is wrong.

cards.f: Effect of a left shift by n
cards.b: Multiplies by 2ⁿ (if no 1s are lost off the left end). Empty places on the right are filled with 0.

cards.f: Effect of a right shift by n
cards.b: Divides by 2ⁿ, keeping the whole-number part. Bits shifted off the right are lost.
Logical fills with 0s. Arithmetic is for signed numbers and keeps the sign bit when shifting right.
Leftmost bit is the sign (1 = negative), rest is the size. Range −127 to +127, with two zeros.
−128 to +127. The leftmost bit has place value −128. Only one zero.

cards.f: How to write a negative number in two's complement
cards.b: Write the positive number in binary, flip every bit, then add 1.
Add the two's complement of b to a (a + (−b)) and ignore any carry out of the left-hand bit.

short.q: Convert the hexadecimal number 3C to 8-bit binary and to denary.
short.model: 3C = 0011 1100 in binary. In denary that is 3 × 16 + 12 = 60.

short.q: Add 00110101 and 00011110 and check your answer in denary.
Explain what is meant by overflow when adding two 8-bit unsigned numbers.
short.model: The answer is bigger than 255, so it needs 9 bits. There is a carry out of the leftmost bit and the stored 8-bit result is wrong.
points: result larger than 255 / too big for 8 bits
carry out of leftmost bit lost, so stored answer is wrong

short.q: Show how to write −45 in 8-bit two's complement.
short.model: 45 = 00101101. Flip the bits to 11010010 and add 1 to get 11010011.

short.q: The 8-bit two's complement number 11110000 (−16) is shifted right by 2 places. Explain which type of shift should be used and give the result.
short.model: An arithmetic shift should be used because it keeps the sign bit. The result is 11111100, which is −4.
points: arithmetic shift keeps the sign bit
